transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-26
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carlos (NovaPay Head of ML), Aisha (Infra), Tom (Platform)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync to review throughput benchmark results after continuous-batching tweaks, discuss concurrency targets and queueing behaviour, and agree on next steps for canary on Dedicated pool. Customer wants stable p50 latency under 200ms with cost close to current baseline.

Topics:
- Benchmarks from last run (tokens/sec, p50/p95)
- Continuous batching params (batch window, timeout)
- Concurrency targets and autoscale behavior
- Queueing / request rejection / backpressure
- Security and VPC peering for Dedicated test

Action items (brief): see action_items metadata above

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: ok hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um this is the weekly POC sync for throughput, I know we have a packed agenda so we'll jump in. Priya and I will run through the numbers then hand over for questions.
[00:24] Priya: hi all, quick note on data quality, we ran three full runs yesterday on the test cluster with the continuous batching flag enabled, and slightly increased the batch_timeout to 30ms to allow larger batches under spiky arrivals. logs and raw traces are in the sheet Ethan will share.
[00:45] Carlos: great — so what's the headline, tokens per second? p50? what's the delta vs last week?
[01:06] Priya: headline: overall throughput improved about 38% on avg for our synthetic traffic shape — we measured ~9.1k tokens/sec aggregate for a single 4-GPU pod (note: this is test cluster numbers), p50 latency moved from ~170ms to ~195ms depending on request length — p95 is still spiking around 620ms on tails when concurrency climbs.
[01:38] Tom: wait p50 got worse? we expected latency to go down with batching, can you unpack that, Priya?
[01:50] Priya: yeah, so there's a tradeoff — when batch sizes increase you amortize kernel overhead so tokens/sec increases, but for short requests the batching window adds queueing delay so p50 sometimes nudges up; the sweet spot we targeted was improving overall cost/token while keeping p50 under 200ms which we are mostly meeting.
[02:18] Aisha: is that with KV cache cold or warm? our production patterns have a warm KV cache most of time.
[02:28] Priya: good call — these runs were mixed; some warm, some cold. We saw warm-cache runs reduce p95 tail by ~150ms, so you should expect better numbers in prod with warm KV cache and prefix caching.
[02:48] Carlos: ok, and what concurrency did you hit when the p95 spikes happened?
[02:55] Priya: spikes correlate with concurrency > 60. Most nice throughput region sits between 20-50 concurrent in our config. we recommend setting a soft max_concurrency target of 45-50 for the Dedicated canary.
[03:16] Ethan: and to clarify, when we say concurrency that's per-pool concurrency target, not per-VM.
[03:25] Tom: got it. so if we set target 50, what's queue behaviour? are requests dropped or queued up? how do we guard against long tails?
[03:38] Priya: Redwood runtime queues requests up to queue_limit (in this test it was 100), beyond that we start shedding (rejecting) at HTTP 429; there's also a fast-fail policy we can enable to return a soft fallback. We recommended increasing queue_limit to 200 for this traffic shape and enabling a small retry with jitter in the client.
[04:05] Carlos: 429s are ok for internal retry, but user-facing latency is sensitive. We need a graceful degradation path — maybe a smaller model fallback?
[04:16] Ethan: yes we demoed model variant fallbacks last week — can automatically route to a cheaper, lower-capacity variant when queueing is high. For NovaPay's workloads we can configure a per-route fallback to our quantized medium model to keep latency bounds at cost tradeoff.
[04:35] Aisha: on the Dedicated canary, network wise we'll need VPC peering and the test SA — I'll action that. Also need the SOC2 summary for security review.
[04:48] Ethan: noted, I'll send the SOC2 link and SSO/SAML checklist after call.
[04:55] Priya: back on tuning — the main knobs that improved throughput were: continuous batching on, batch_timeout 30ms, adaptive kernel selection left at default, and a slightly more aggressive pre-warm probe to avoid cold KV cache. For your traffic we saw best cost/perf with concurrency 35-50 depending on request length distribution.
[05:20] Carlos: how deterministic are these numbers? if we run a different day will results vary a lot?
[05:30] Priya: there is variance, we saw +-8% across runs on same cluster; production variance will be larger due to multi-tenant noise on shared infra and network jitter; Dedicated reduces that noise.
[05:46] Tom: cost question — do we have an estimate of cost per 1M tokens with these settings vs current baseline?
[05:54] Ethan: rough ballpark from our test: cost/token decreased about 32% with continuous batching due to higher utilization, so 1M tokens cost went down accordingly but we'll provide a clearer breakdown in the sheet.
[06:12] Carlos: ok good. Next, can you walk through the queueing timeline when we get a sudden spike? like 10x burst for 30s.
[06:23] Priya: yes — when a large burst arrives the runtime's continuous batching aggregates requests up to max_batch and if concurrency is saturated requests queue. If queue_limit reached, we start 429s. For a short 30s burst we observed a 15-30% drop in p50 but long tails p95 spiked; recommended mitigation: enable short-lived autoscale burst capacity (we can configure Dedicated pool to add 1-2 extra GPU nodes for 2-3 minutes), plus client-side rate-limiting and exponential backoff.
[07:01] Tom: is autoscale fast enough for 30s bursts?
[07:06] Priya: typical container scale-up takes ~90-150s depending on infra; for true sub-1min bursts you'd rely on burst capacity that's pre-allocated (reserve) or warm standby nodes. We can set a small reserved burst for the canary.
[07:21] Carlos: ok let's discuss the canary plan; recommended config?
[07:27] Priya: suggested canary: Dedicated pool with 4x A10s (or equivalent) configured with max_concurrency 50, batch_timeout 30ms, queue_limit 200, burst_reserve 1 node, run 1 hour with traffic replay of 1x and 2x production for 15m each. We'll collect p50/p95, tokens/sec, and per-route error rates.
[07:50] Ethan: we'll also enable the fallback model route so if queueing > threshold we route to quantized-medium to keep latency bounded.
[07:58] Aisha: sounds good — I can set up VPC peering tonight and create the test SA, will share the peering CID and service account by EOD.
[08:09] Carlos: what's the instrumentation level we get? can we see token-level latency and per-request KV cache hits?
[08:18] Priya: yes, Redwood console provides per-request traces with KV cache hit flags (though sometimes the exported field name is 'KV cash' in older logs, sorry for the typo in the sheet). We'll attach the trace links.
[08:34] Tom: any security blockers for the Dedicated canary?
[08:38] Ethan: none from Redwood side, but we'll need the peering and an approved service account. Also we'll share the SOC2 summary and support an on-site audit if required; NovaPay can also request encryption details — we support KMS/HSM integrations.
[08:54] Carlos: perfect. Regarding fallbacks, how do we measure quality regression when we route to smaller model? we need an eval set.
[09:03] Priya: yes please share a small eval prompt set (50-100 prompts) that reflect NovaPay user queries; we'll run A/B and produce a delta report and quality metrics.
[09:13] Carlos: will do.
[09:16] Ethan: quick note — we saw one dropped run due to a config typo where the max_batch was set too low; logs show frequent small batches. we've fixed that in the sheet and the run that matters is run #3 in the spreadsheet.
[09:31] Aisha: small thing — your docs mention autoscale policies, what's the unit for burst_reserve? nodes or GPUs?
[09:38] Priya: burst_reserve is in nodes; each node contains x GPUs depending on instance type. we'll include exact mapping in the canary doc.
[09:46] Carlos: ok I want to confirm the acceptance criteria for the POC success: p50 <200ms for 90% of traffic, p95 <700ms, no more than 0.5% 429s, and cost within 25% of the cost target.
[10:03] Ethan: should we capture that as SLO in the canary doc?
[10:07] Tom: yes let's make that the canary acceptance criteria.
[10:11] Priya: we'll include those thresholds and set monitoring alerts in the Redwood console during the canary so we can abort automatically if thresholds exceed.
[10:20] Carlos: good. Any other risks?
[10:23] Priya: main risk is traffic shape mismatch — if your prod traffic is more tail-heavy (longer requests) batching helps less for latency sensitive flows. Also if KV cache is frequently cold then tails worsen; that's why we ask for production trace.
[10:40] Ethan: ok to recap next steps: I (Ethan) will send SOC2 + SSO checklist + updated spreadsheet by tomorrow; Priya will push config changes to test cluster (batch_timeout 30ms, max_concurrency 50, queue_limit 200) and run the 100k-request benchmark and share results; Carlos/Aisha will provide prod trace and set up VPC peering; Tom will schedule the Dedicated canary for 2026-09-02.
[11:05] Carlos: yep that's good. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[11:09] Priya: none; just need the peering and SA.
[11:13] Tom: ok I'll book the canary window and invite the right infra folks.
[11:18] Ethan: great thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email.
[11:22] (end)

Notes: transcript includes small transcription errors and shorthand typical of Fireflies exports; please refer to attached benchmark spreadsheet and trace links for raw logs and run-by-run numbers.
